A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same study and contain readable main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices. The appendix interface screenshots were also inspected and matched.

before.justification: V2 reports original human-study results from 72 analyzed treatment participants and an additional 18-person repetition-control study in Appendix F.

after.justification: V3 reports original decision accuracy, confidence-weighted accuracy, reliance behavior, and survey results for 90 analyzed participants across five conditions.

M1.justification: The four feedback procedures retain the same XCOMET error highlights, Llama-3.3 explanations and ASKQE question-answer tables, and Google backtranslation. Their generation procedures, prompts, and feedback-decision proxies remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 20 selected English-Spanish CONTRATICO examples, COVID-19 translation-shareability task, and English-speaking participant population. The repetition-control scenario already appears in v2 Appendix F.

E2.justification: The four feedback conditions and no-feedback repetition control are already compared in v2 Appendix F and Table 3. Their integration into v3 Figure 3 and Table 5 does not introduce a new comparator.

E3.justification: V2 describes random assignment among four treatments plus a separately recruited control study; v3 describes random assignment among five conditions. This revises the stated allocation protocol. The reported 91 participants equal v2's 73 plus 18, so the PDFs do not establish additional recruitment or rerunning.

E4.justification: The repetition-effect check, shareability breakdown, switching analysis, survey analysis, and participant-comment analysis are retained. V2 Appendix F is incorporated into v3's main discussion rather than replaced by a new robustness or supplementary analysis.

E5.justification: Control estimates previously reported with standard errors in v2 Table 3 receive 95% confidence intervals in v3 Table 5, while the standalone standard-error table is removed. Paired t-tests, mixed-effects ANOVA, and Bonferroni correction remain unchanged.

E6.justification: V2 Appendix F says all feedback conditions significantly outperform the control; v3 Section 4.1 excludes error highlights, consistent with its Figure 3. V3 Table 5 also adds pooled control accuracy and CWA values of 0.609 and 0.177. Existing treatment means and detailed reliance results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations 1–2 replace E in averaging denominators with |E|, clarifying cardinality without changing the intended mathematics. Feedback-proxy definitions, Equation 4, and decision-transition categories are retained; no substantive theoretical development is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims: three feedback types improve both decision accuracy and appropriate reliance, implicit feedback generally performs better, and QA tables are especially effective. Incorporating the existing control changes the study summary rather than these contributions.

C2.justification: Interpretations concerning repetition, cognitive burden, user agency, and difficulty detecting problematic translations are retained. The limitations concerning presentation differences, target-language users, restricted coverage, and synthetic errors also remain substantively unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix C.2 reports combined recruitment totals of 205 screened and 123 invited, replacing 165 and 98, and revises costs and completion-time summaries. V2's separate control completion time is omitted. Model specifications, prompts, hardware, and code-access information remain unchanged.

R1.justification: V3 adds Agrawal et al. (2022), Briakou et al. (2023), Carpuat et al. (2025), and two Xiao et al. (2025) works. Somers (2005) and several reliance-study references accompanying the former learning-effects appendix are removed. The overall research positioning remains stable.

P1.justification: V3 integrates the control-study account into the main methods and results, separates control and treatment survey descriptions, and renumbers Detailed Results from Appendix G to F. Local wording and heading edits accompany this limited reorganization; most prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1 adds the control option, and Figure 3 adds control bars and significance brackets. Table 1 replaces feedback icons with names and includes the control; v2 Table 3 is consolidated into other displays. Figures 4–7 retain their visual content.

improvement.justification: V3 makes the existing control evidence easier to assess, supplies control confidence intervals, and narrows the significance statement to exclude error highlights. These provide limited improvements in clarity and reporting consistency. The unexplained shift from separately recruited control participants to five-way random assignment remains a weakness in the revised design description.
